executive_summary.description: A high-level overview of the key findings regarding the accessibility, coverage, and fragmentation of arts and cultural event data in Richmond, Virginia.

platform_name.description: The name of the calendar software platform used by CultureWorks.

provides_structured_data.description: Indicates whether structured data feeds are available.

available_formats.description: A list of the available structured data formats (e.g., ICS, RSS, JSON API).

data_sharing_terms.description: A summary of the terms of use or any policies regarding data sharing and API usage.

platform_name.description: The name of the event platform (e.g., CultureWorks, Eventbrite, Style Weekly).

estimated_monthly_events.description: An estimate of the number of arts and culture events listed per month.

coverage_focus.description: The primary focus of the platform's event listings (e.g., broad arts and culture, ticketed events, specific genres).

data_accessibility.description: Notes on how accessible the event data is for aggregation (e.g., offers API, requires scraping).

institution_name.description: The name of the flagship cultural institution.

has_machine_readable_feed.description: Indicates whether the institution provides a machine-readable event feed.

feed_formats.description: The formats available for the event feed, if any (e.g., ICS, RSS, Google Calendar).

calendar_url.description: The direct URL to the institution's event calendar page.

flagship_institution_data_feeds.description: A list detailing the availability of machine-readable event feeds (such as ICS, RSS, or JSON) for Richmond's flagship cultural institutions, including the VMFA, ICA at VCU, Richmond Symphony, Richmond Ballet, Virginia Rep, and the Modlin Center.

audience_event_discovery_channels.description: An analysis based on available survey data and research into how Richmond residents actually discover arts and cultural events. This covers the primary channels that drive attendance, such as social media, word-of-mouth, email newsletters, and specific publications.

current_status.description: The current operational status of the dorichmond.com website.

parent_network.description: The parent media company, DoStuff Media, that operated the site.

licensing_opportunity.description: An assessment of whether a licensing opportunity exists to revive the Richmond presence.

contact_method.description: Information on how to contact the parent network regarding a new city launch.

us_regional_event_data_standards.description: Research into case studies of US cities that have attempted to implement a shared regional events data standard across tourism boards, arts councils, and media outlets. This includes any findings on existing Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) or collaborative frameworks.

prevalence_of_unstructured_events.description: An analytical estimate of the percentage of Richmond arts events that exist only on unstructured platforms like Facebook Events or on physical flyers, with no corresponding structured web presence on a major calendar.

cultureworks_platform_details.description: Specific details about the CultureWorks calendar platform, identifying it as Localist and explaining the features this platform offers, such as embeddable widgets, email digests, and various subscription options.

style_weekly_calendar_details.description: Information on the structure and data accessibility of Style Weekly's event calendar, including an assessment of its user interface and whether it offers any machine-readable subscription or export features.

eventbrite_as_data_source.description: Analysis of using Eventbrite as a data source for Richmond arts events, including methods for searching and the challenges of programmatically isolating arts-specific events from other categories within the platform.

facebook_events_as_data_source.description: A discussion on the significant role of Facebook Events in the Richmond arts scene, highlighting its importance as a major data source while also detailing the technical and legal challenges associated with scraping or integrating this unstructured data.

source_name.description: The name of the data source (e.g., CultureWorks, VMFA, Facebook).

source_type.description: The type of platform (e.g., Community Calendar, Institutional Site, Social Media).

data_accessibility.description: How the data can be accessed (e.g., ICS/RSS Feed, API, Web Scraping).

notes.description: Key characteristics or challenges associated with this data source.

summary_of_key_data_sources.description: A consolidated list of the primary digital platforms and institutional websites that serve as the main sources for arts and cultural event listings in the Richmond area.

data_aggregation_challenges.description: A concluding summary of the main difficulties and fragmentation issues one would face when attempting to build a comprehensive, aggregated arts event dataset for the Richmond region.

recommendations_for_data_aggregator.description: Strategic recommendations and potential next steps for an organization or individual looking to create a centralized, comprehensive arts and culture event aggregator for Richmond, based on the research findings.
